title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on Disclosure of Information in Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the Provisions on the Disclosure of Information in Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases (Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2016] No. 19

To: the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Supreme People's Court hereby prints and distributes the Provisions on the Disclosure of Information in Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases (Trial Implementation). Please implement them diligently in light of the actual conditions in your respective localities.

July 26, 2016

Provisions on the Disclosure of Information in Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases (Trial Implementation)

For the purposes of enhancing the transparency and credibility of the adjudication of bankruptcy cases, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and in light of the actual work of the people's courts, with respect to the disclosure of information in bankruptcy cases.

Article 1 The Supreme People's Court shall establish a National Enterprise Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network (hereinafter referred to as the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network). Information relating to the trial process of bankruptcy cases (including cases of bankruptcy restructuring, bankruptcy liquidation, and bankruptcy composition) as well as announcements, legal documents, debtor information, and other information related to bankruptcy proceedings shall be uniformly published on the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network.

The people's courts and the bankruptcy administrators designated by the people's courts shall use the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network to promptly disclose information related to bankruptcy proceedings.

Article 2 The disclosure of information in bankruptcy cases shall take disclosure as the principle and non-disclosure as the exception. All information that does not involve state secrets or personal privacy shall be disclosed in accordance with the law. As to debtor information involving trade secrets, the bankruptcy administrator may, without prejudice to the legitimate rights and interests of the creditors and the debtor, disclose such information to the restructuring investor through an agreement with the restructuring investor.

Article 3 The people's court shall, in accordance with the law, disclose the following information of a bankruptcy case:

(1) Information on the nodes of the trial process;
(2) Various announcements published by the people's court in the bankruptcy proceedings;
(3) Legal documents of the bankruptcy proceedings prepared by the people's court;
(4) Other information that the people's court deems should be disclosed.

Article 4 The bankruptcy administrator shall, in accordance with the law, disclose the following information of a bankruptcy case:

(1) Debtor information;
(2) Announcements soliciting or recruiting restructuring investors;
(3) Information on the work nodes of the bankruptcy administrator;
(4) Other announcements published by the bankruptcy administrator in the bankruptcy proceedings;
(5) Legal documents of the bankruptcy proceedings prepared by the bankruptcy administrator;
(6) The restructuring plan approved by the people's court by ruling, the plan for distribution of bankruptcy property recognized by the people's court, and the composition agreement.

Other information that the bankruptcy administrator deems should be disclosed may be disclosed upon approval by the people's court.

Article 5 The bankruptcy administrator shall promptly disclose the following debtor information through the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network:

(1) Industrial and commercial registration information;
(2) The annual report for the most recent year;
(3) The balance sheet for the most recent year;
(4) Basic information on the litigation or arbitration cases involved.

Article 6 The restructuring investor may interact with the bankruptcy administrator through the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network. The bankruptcy administrator may, in accordance with an agreement with the restructuring investor, disclose the following debtor information to the restructuring investor:

(1) Information on assets and business operations;
(2) Detailed information on litigation or arbitration cases involved;
(3) Other information needed by the restructuring investor.

Article 7 The people's court and the bankruptcy administrator may publish announcements relating to the bankruptcy proceedings on the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network.

Where the people's court or the bankruptcy administrator publishes announcements on other media, it shall simultaneously publish the announcements on the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network. Announcements published by the people's court or the bankruptcy administrator on the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network shall have legal effect.

Article 8 With the consent of the person subject to service, the people's court may, through the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network, serve legal documents relating to the bankruptcy proceedings, except for written rulings, by electronic mail, mobile communication, or other means capable of confirming receipt.

Where service is made by the means specified in the preceding paragraph, the date on which the electronic mail or mobile communication reaches the specific system of the person subject to service shall be deemed the date of service.

Article 9 An applicant may, after real-name registration on the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network, apply for case filing by appointment and submit electronic versions of relevant materials. After examination and approval, the people's court shall notify the applicant to come to the case filing counter of the people's court to complete the case filing registration.

Article 10 A creditor may, after real-name registration on the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network, declare claims and submit electronic versions of relevant evidence. Declaring claims online shall have the same legal effect as declaring claims by other means.

Where a creditor declares its claims in writing to the bankruptcy administrator, the bankruptcy administrator shall upload the electronic versions of the claim declaration form and related evidence to the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network.

Article 11 The people's court or the bankruptcy administrator may convene a creditors' meeting and conduct voting on relevant matters through the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Case Information Network. The voting results formed by online voting shall have the same legal effect as the voting results formed by on-site voting.

A creditor may choose to vote on-site or online, but after making a choice, it may no longer vote by any other means. Where voting is conducted by other means, such voting shall be null and void.

Article 12 The provisions of these Provisions shall apply mutatis mutandis to compulsory liquidation cases of companies tried by the people's court.

Article 13 These Provisions shall come into effect on August 1, 2016. Bankruptcy cases accepted after the effective date of these Provisions, as well as bankruptcy cases that have not yet been concluded before the effective date, shall be governed by these Provisions.
